items.title: Unital banach algebra
items.strategy: Specify associative complex algebra with bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative complete norm and nonzero identity of norm one. The zero algebra is excluded.

items.title: Neumann series
items.strategy: Sum the geometric series in norm, multiply finite partial sums on each side, and bound the remainder by ||a||^(N+1)/(1-||a||).

items.strategy: Verify R(z)-R(w)=(w-z)R(z)R(w) and R(z,a)-R(z,b)=R(z,a)(a-b)R(z,b) by direct multiplication.

items.title: Resolvent is banach valued holomorphic

items.title: Spectrum is nonempty compact and norm bounded
items.strategy: If the spectrum were empty, apply each bounded functional to the resolvent. It is bounded on compact disks and tends to zero at infinity, hence is zero by scalar Liouville. Dual separation contradicts invertibility. Compactness follows from closedness and the Neumann norm bound. Record HB inherited through dual separation.

items.title: Submultiplicative root limit
items.statement: If u_n>=0 and u_{m+n}<=u_m u_n, then lim_{n→∞}u_n^{1/n}=inf_{n>=1}u_n^{1/n}, with the zero-term case included.
items.strategy: Use the N-indexed sequence v_j=u_{j+1}^{1/(j+1)}. Handle a zero term; otherwise divide n=qk+r, bound by t^n D_k for fixed positive t=u_k^(1/k), and apply the shifted constant-root lemma to D_k^(1/(j+1)). Compare limsup and liminf of v only.

items.title: Spectral radius formula
items.strategy: Treat a=0 first. For a nonzero, use h(z)=(1-za)^-1 on |z|<1/Rprime with r(a)<Rprime<R, then scalar Cauchy on |z|=1/R. Uniform Neumann tails and ML justify coefficient extraction. Dual norm gives ||a^n||≤C_R R^n with C_R>0. Use the explicit zero-based root sequence and its submultiplicative limit; polynomial spectral mapping gives the reverse inequality.

items.title: Canonical Banach complexification of a real Banach space
items.strategy: On X×X use complex scalar multiplication and the rotation-supremum norm. Prove the norm axioms and max(||x||,||y||)<=||x+iy||_C<=||x||+||y||, so completeness follows componentwise. For T_C(x+iy)=Tx+iTy, rotations give ||T_C||<=||T|| and the real copy gives equality. For any other compatible Banach complexification Z with an isometric real embedding j, conjugation, and fixed real copy, z=j(x)+ij(y) uniquely and x=(z+conj(z))/2, y=(z-conj(z))/(2i). These formulas and the triangle inequality bound the canonical intertwiner and its inverse; it is therefore a bounded complex-linear isomorphism intertwining all complexified operators. It is isometric only when the comparison model carries the same rotation-supremum norm.
items.statement: For a real Banach space X, X_C=X⊕iX with ||x+iy||_C=sup_theta ||cos(theta)x-sin(theta)y|| is a complex Banach space; X embeds isometrically and every bounded real T extends complex-linearly with the same norm. Every compatible Banach complexification with continuous conjugation and the same fixed real copy is canonically boundedly complex-linearly isomorphic to this model, and the isomorphism intertwines complexified operators; it is isometric when the other model uses the same rotation-supremum norm.

items.title: Complexification and spectrum of a real operator
items.strategy: Use the preceding rotation-supremum complexification and T_C(x+iy)=Tx+iTy. If a different compatible complexification is used, the preceding canonical bounded complex-linear isomorphism conjugates the two extended operators. Since bounded conjugacy preserves invertibility of lambda I-T_C and its inverse, it preserves the resolvent, spectrum, and spectral radius. No false isometric uniqueness is required.

items.title: Gelfand mazur
items.strategy: A spectral value lambda for a forces a-lambda*1=0 in a division algebra. Scalar inclusion is an algebra isomorphism and is isometric because the unit norm is one.

items.title: Banach algebra valued contour integral
items.strategy: Use tagged Riemann sums for each C1 segment; completeness and uniform continuity make them converge, and subdivision/reparametrization proves well-definedness before extending to finite cycles. Uniform step approximants also prove strong measurability and L1 convergence, so the same sums converge to the Bochner integral of t↦f(gamma(t))gamma'(t); this establishes, rather than postpones, agreement with FA-12.

Banach-algebra integrals are the special case.

items.title: Contour integral commutes with bounded linear maps
items.strategy: Apply a bounded map to Riemann sums and pass to the limit; include the length-times-supremum norm bound.

items.title: Banach valued cauchy integral vanishes
items.strategy: Assume continuity and weak holomorphy on an open set and a cycle null-homologous there. Scalar Cauchy annihilates every bounded functional of the integral, then dual separation annihilates the vector integral.

items.title: Admissible cycle around a compact plane set
items.statement: For compact K⊂U with U open in C, there is a finite polygonal cycle Gamma⊂U\K with index 1 near K and 0 outside U; two such cycles may be chosen with separated traces and nested buffers.
items.strategy: Choose two sufficiently fine square grids subordinate to positive-distance buffers K⊂V1⊂cl(V1)⊂V2⊂cl(V2)⊂U. Take the finite squares meeting each compact closure, orient their union boundaries, and cancel internal edges. Rectangle winding-number additivity gives index one on the inner set and zero outside the outer union; perturb grid origins to avoid K and to make the two traces disjoint.

items.title: Holomorphic functional calculus
items.strategy: Assume AC and use compactness of the nonempty spectrum to place it inside the neighbourhood U and apply the admissible-cycle lemma. The cycle lies in U minus sigma(a), has index one near sigma(a), and index zero outside U. Define the integral for a representative of the germ; notation f(a) becomes canonical only after the following independence lemma.

items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited through the declared compact-spectrum supplier; construction of the finite admissible cycle and the integral uses no further choice.

items.title: Holomorphic functional calculus is contour independent
items.strategy: The difference of admissible cycles is null-homologous in U minus sigma(a). Scalarize the integrand and apply the Banach Cauchy lemma. Also prove independence of the chosen germ representative.

items.title: Holomorphic functional calculus homomorphism
items.strategy: Construct two separated nested admissible cycles, use the ordered resolvent identity, and justify double integrals by uniform Riemann sums. Prove unit and coordinate function identities using a large circle; polynomials and inverses follow.

items.statement: Assume AC. The holomorphic functional calculus is a unital algebra homomorphism, sends the coordinate function to a, and extends polynomial and local inverse evaluation.

items.title: Holomorphic spectral mapping
items.strategy: If mu avoids f(sigma(a)), use 1/(f-mu). For mu=f(lambda), divide f(z)-mu by z-lambda with its removable value at lambda; commuting product invertibility forces the reverse inclusion. This works also for constant components.

items.title: Riesz spectral projection
items.strategy: For a clopen spectral subset E apply the calculus to its locally constant characteristic function; identify the contour formula.

items.statement: Assume AC. For a clopen E⊂sigma(a), the Riesz projection P_E is the holomorphic-calculus value of the locally constant characteristic function of E, equivalently its resolvent contour integral.
items.axiom_audit: Full AC is inherited from the declared holomorphic-functional-calculus supplier; the definition itself uses no further choice.

items.title: Riesz spectral projection properties
items.strategy: For T in B(X), multiplicativity of the calculus gives P_E^2=P_E and TP_E=P_ET. A bounded projection has closed range and kernel and yields X=ran(P_E) direct-sum ker(P_E); both summands are T-invariant. Restrict the resolvent/calculus to each nonzero summand and use spectral mapping for the locally constant characteristic function to obtain spectra E and sigma(T)\E. If either spectral part is empty, the corresponding summand is zero and no spectrum is assigned to its zero operator algebra under the normalized nonzero-algebra convention.

items.statement: Assume AC. If T∈B(X) and E is clopen in sigma(T), then P_E is a bounded idempotent commuting with T and X=ran(P_E)⊕ker(P_E). On each nonzero summand the corresponding restriction of T has spectrum E or sigma(T)\E, respectively; an empty spectral part gives the zero summand, to which no spectrum is assigned under the normalized nonzero-algebra convention.

items.title: Calkin algebra
items.strategy: For a complex Banach space X, first use completeness of B(X). The compact operators form a closed two-sided linear ideal by the three declared compact-operator suppliers, so quotient multiplication is well-defined and submultiplicative and quotient completeness follows under Countable Choice. If X is infinite-dimensional, I is not compact, hence its coset is nonzero. Its quotient norm is at most ||I||=1, while every nonzero unit in a submultiplicative normed algebra has norm at least one, so the quotient unit has norm exactly one. Finite-dimensional X gives the zero quotient and is treated separately rather than called normalized unital.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space X, the Calkin algebra is B(X)/K(X) with quotient norm and unit I+K(X); it is a normalized unital complex Banach algebra.
items.axiom_audit: Countable Choice is inherited in norm-limit compactness and quotient completeness and explicitly selects a sequence from the norm closure. No stronger choice is used.

items.title: Atkinson in calkin algebra language
items.strategy: Quotient invertibility is precisely existence of a bounded two-sided parametrix modulo compact operators. Keep the infinite-dimensional convention explicit; no new Fredholm proof is hidden here.

items.title: Boundary of spectrum lies in approximate point spectrum

If T-lambda were bounded below uniformly nearby, the nearby inverses would be uniformly bounded and a Neumann perturbation would invert T-lambda, contradiction. Normalize inverse images to construct approximate eigenvectors, recording countable choice.

title: Banach Algebras Spectrum and Holomorphic Functional Calculus — Examples

items.title: Continuous functions form a commutative banach algebra
items.statement: For nonempty compact Hausdorff K prove C(K,C) is a unital commutative Banach algebra under the supremum norm; spectrum of f is f(K).
items.strategy: A continuous complex function on compact K has compact, hence bounded, image, so the supremum norm is finite. Pointwise operations give a commutative algebra, ||fg||_infty<=||f||_infty||g||_infty, and the constant one has norm one. A sup-norm Cauchy sequence is uniformly Cauchy, hence converges uniformly to a complex function; uniform-limit continuity proves completeness. If lambda is outside f(K), compactness gives positive distance from lambda to f(K), so 1/(lambda-f) is a bounded continuous inverse of lambda-f. If lambda=f(x), evaluation at x rules out an inverse. Thus sigma(f)=f(K).

items.title: Bounded operators form a noncommutative banach algebra
items.statement: For every nonzero complex Banach space X, B(X) is a normalized unital Banach algebra; B(C^2) is noncommutative.
items.strategy: Composition is bilinear and associative and satisfies ||ST||<=||S||||T||. The identity is the unit and has norm one because X is nonzero. Invoke completeness of the bounded-operator space to obtain a Banach algebra. In B(C^2), the matrix units satisfy E_12E_21=E_11 while E_21E_12=E_22, proving noncommutativity.

items.title: Spectrum in a finite dimensional matrix algebra
items.statement: For n>=1, give M_n(C) its Euclidean operator norm. It is a unital Banach algebra, and the spectrum of A is exactly {lambda∈C:det(lambda I-A)=0}.
items.strategy: The Euclidean operator norm is submultiplicative, the identity has norm one, and finite-dimensional completeness makes M_n(C) a Banach algebra. If det(lambda I-A) is nonzero, the adjugate identity supplies the inverse divided by the determinant. Conversely, if lambda I-A has a matrix inverse, determinant multiplicativity forces its determinant to be nonzero. This proves the stated spectral formula without importing an undeclared finite-dimensional spectral theorem.

items.title: Spectrum of a multiplication operator
items.statement: Assume AC. Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a nonzero sigma-finite measure space and m:X→C an essentially bounded measurable function. On complex L^2(mu), the multiplication operator M_m is bounded and sigma(M_m)=essran(m), where essran(m)={lambda∈C:mu({x:|m(x)-lambda|<epsilon})>0 for every epsilon>0}. For the zero measure space, L^2 is the zero space and the normalized nonzero-algebra spectral convention does not apply.
items.strategy: Multiplication by m respects almost-everywhere equivalence classes, is measurable, and satisfies ||M_m f||_2<=||m||_infinity||f||_2. If lambda is outside the displayed essential range, |m-lambda| is bounded below almost everywhere, so multiplication by (m-lambda)^{-1} is a bounded two-sided inverse. If lambda is in the essential range, A_n={|m-lambda|<1/n} has positive measure. From a fixed sigma-finite exhaustion X=union_k E_k with mu(E_k)<infinity, choose the first k for which A_n intersect E_k has positive measure; its normalized indicator is in L^2 and satisfies ||(M_m-lambda)f_n||_2<1/n, ruling out invertibility. AC is inherited from the bounded-operator algebra supplier and implies Countable Choice for completeness. Multiplication and composition are proved directly on representatives; nonzero L2 follows from a finite positive-measure member of the exhaustion.

references.title: Theo Bühler and Dietmar A. Salamon, Functional Analysis

items.title: Spectrum of the unilateral shift
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For S e_n=e_(n+1) on ell2(N0), the spectrum is the closed unit disk, the point spectrum is empty, the residual and compression spectra are the open disk, and the continuous and approximate point spectra are the unit circle. Prove the lower bound inside the disk, a coordinate-inner-product annihilator of the range there, and normalized long blocks at the boundary.
items.strategy: Use counting measure on N0 (identified explicitly with N) and the complex-Lp supplier to obtain complex ell2, its first-variable-linear coordinate inner product, and completeness; counting measure makes almost-everywhere equality pointwise. The right shift is an isometry and has no eigenvalues. Outside the closed disk invert by a Neumann series. For |lambda|<1, the vector (1,conj(lambda),conj(lambda)^2,...) annihilates the range of S-lambda I under the coordinate inner product, while the coordinate recursion gives a uniform lower bound, so these points are residual/compression but not approximate. On |lambda|=1, normalized long geometric blocks are approximate eigenvectors and the range is dense but not onto. items.strategy: Define A(D) as the functions continuous on the closed disk and holomorphic in its interior, with the supremum norm. items.title: Gelfand transform of ell one of z
items.strategy: Fix explicit bijections N↔Z and N↔Z^2 and define ell1(Z) and convolution coordinatewise. Tonelli applied to |a_j b_{n-j}| gives ||a*b||_1<=||a||_1||b||_1 and absolute convergence of every convolution coordinate. Tonelli again gives absolute convergence of the relevant double and triple arrays; applying real double-series Fubini to real and imaginary parts justifies all regroupings and proves associativity and character multiplicativity. Complex completeness gives coordinate limits, while finite partial-sum bounds and a fixed Cauchy-tail estimate prove completeness of ell1(Z). The point mass delta_0 is the unit. Since delta_1 is invertible with inverse delta_{-1}, every character sends it to z with |z|=1. Transport P_N by the explicit isometry U(a)_k=a_{b(k)} and define Q_N=U^{-1}P_NU. This transported finite-truncation density and continuity give chi(a)=sum_n a_n z^n; conversely this absolutely convergent Laurent series defines a character. Its tail is uniformly bounded by the ell1 tail, so the circle-to-character map is continuous; evaluation on delta_1 is its continuous inverse (equivalently use compact-to-Hausdorff), giving the claimed topological parameterization. The inverse-closed Wiener consequence remains only a separate orientation remark.
